content.comment_body: I need help. My input doors aren’t functioning, not even through the software. Could there be a safe mode on the [product_name]?

Hi, The [product_name] operates in four modes: No Program, Stop, Run, and Defective. Could you provide more details about your situation, such as the [product_name] version and how the device is wired?

Hi, thanks for helping. The model I’m using is [product_name], article number [article_no]. Currently, there’s nothing connected except 230VAC power. I connect with a USB cable and use the software, but the simulation doesn’t allow pressing the input switches. Even when I apply a 230V pulse directly to an input, it isn’t working now. I was running tests with the device upside-down against the table and wondered if a button got stuck and blocked the inputs.

You’re using a physical [product_name] and trying to activate inputs through the simulation? That won’t work. For real hardware, use Online Test (the button below the simulation one) to view live input states.
Even if I connect a 230V pulse to an input, the controller doesn’t respond.
Is this happening on all inputs? What voltage did you use—was it identical to the device’s power supply, or from another source?
I applied the same voltage as the power supply. Even with just one connected input, it still doesn’t work.
When you view the input screen, do you see the state of your input change? Refer to the attached image.
No, the input states don’t change.

It seems likely that the [product_name] hardware is defective. Try using the second input group (starting at I5). If none of the inputs register on the display (and the device is in Run mode), then it’s probable the hardware has failed. Only you know the full history of its usage.
No change—fifth input is still inactive, even though I didn’t use it before. HELP! The inputs are rated for 230VAC, which I used, so I can’t see what could have damaged them.

analysis.insight_summary: Users report that none of the digital inputs respond—neither through the connected software nor when applying the specified voltage. The community helps clarify the difference between simulation and live hardware testing, but ultimately hardware failure is suspected. The conversation highlights difficulty distinguishing hardware malfunctions from incorrect software usage.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects the device's digital inputs to react either to software actions or direct voltage. They seek guidance on safe mode options and troubleshooting steps for unresponsive hardware. Reliable information about the device's condition and troubleshooting support are requested.
